The two activities I engage in lately are kayaking and bicycling. Both get you out in the sun and fresh air. Both are inexpensive.

For kayaking, what you need is a kayak (duh!), a double-sided paddle, and some water to paddle around on. A nice little recreational kayak with an open cockpit will cost about $600, maybe less -- but you should buy a little quality. You don't need a hard-shell kayak. They are more expensive, heavier, bigger, and very fragile. Bang them hard and you have a hole in them. The recreational kayaks are made of a kind of plastic that is almost indestructable. Paddles will run you around $100, give or take, for a half-decent one. And you'll need a cheap life jacket. That's it. Forever. None of these things wear out. They will be as good ten years from now as the day you buy them. You can put the kayak in the back of your pickup or on roofracks or sticking out the back window of your SUV, and take it anywhere. You can paddle in lakes, rivers, or on the ocean. It's ten times more stable than a canoe when you are sitting in it, although it is a bit tricky to get into and out of.

OK, on to bicycling. I've got a 29er mountain bike. I use it mostly on back roads, although I have had it on trails. If you are going to ride in the suburbs, or the city, or on quiet country roads, you probably want a crossover bike. If you want to do dirt roads and trails, get a mountain bike. If you are into highway riding, get a road bike. You don't need to pay more than around $200 for any of these types. If you look around, and buy on sale, $200 will get you an aluminum frame, Shimano derailleurs, and disk brakes. If you aren't an experienced bike rider you will want a bike with an upright seating position -- one where the seat is lower than the handlebars, not higher.

Biking is a great way to stay in shape and lose weight. You can push the bike home if you get a flat tire or have a mechanical problem. You can pick it up and carry it across obstacles such as fences or streams. It becomes like an extension of your body, and there's always more to learn, and more skills to acquire, so it stays interesting.

Anyway, that's what I do in my spare time, and I can't think of too many recreational activities that cost less or are healthier for you.
